== Course of events ==

After the Guardian of the Gate removed their green spectacles and sent the travelers off with good wishes, having told the Scarecrow he must return to rule the City once Dorothy is safely home, the group continued on their way. The Tin Woodman chopped through a branch to clear a path, and the party reached a high wall of white china beyond the wood. It was in this stretch of the journey that the Tin Woodman, Scarecrow, and Lion spoke admiringly of Oz, praising him for what he had done for them. Dorothy, however, did not join in their praise; privately, she forgave Oz for failing to keep his promise to her, keeping her feelings to herself rather than voicing them to her companions.

This quiet moment of reflection came before the group pressed onward toward the wall of white china, where Dorothy would soon meet a china Princess who refused to be carried away, and where the Lion would later smash a china church with his tail while jumping onto a second wall. Dorothy's private act of forgiveness marked a turning point in her feelings toward Oz, even as the Tin Woodman, Scarecrow, and Lion remained openly grateful to him.
